pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/athena/proving/sandbox/__init__.py:9 This is a standalone CLI spike that polls a remote sandbox REST service. No module outside the package imports it, and a search of the context's directories for hook, plugin, middleware, run_turn and entry_point found nothing, so there is no agent loop, hook chain or contributed code to assemble.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/proving/sandbox/client.py:248 The long-running remote operation is polled synchronously by a CLI script, not by a model loop, so the precondition (model-visible remote work that outlives a turn) does not hold.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/athena/daemon/routes.py:678 The gate's per-turn policy inputs (disabled_origins, gated_origins, gated_tools) are read from the request body. A malformed or missing list silently becomes an empty set (routes.py:767-768), so switched-off apps become addressable again and first-sight apps lose their forced gating, instead of the turn failing loudly.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/daemon/routes.py:678 Custody itself holds: only the token-holding shell writes these lists. But a malformed guard input degrades to the permissive default, which is the technique's question 4 (absent-guard-is-loud). Only an over-long list is refused.

src/athena/daemon/routes.py:514 The service door refuses any manifest with origin_kind other than host. Connectors, the only contributions with in-process executors, register in process, so the authenticated service tier cannot name code.

src/athena/daemon/routes.py:836 The setup tools resolve from the session's own key, not from an environment slot. One disabled-origins set then drives both the prompt filter and the gate's refusal for that turn.
src/athena/daemon/routes.py:307 Every route is host code (base routes, connector routes). No contribution mounts handlers, so there is no mount order to defend. The table also refuses duplicates.
